section_summary: This section documents U.S. government evaluations, military proposals, and occupation policies concerning Japanese writing system reform between March 1945 and January 1949. Early proposals, including a 1945 Civil Affairs Staging Area paper urging the exclusive use of katakana, were rejected by the State Department as linguistically unsound and impractical due to Chinese-derived homophones. Subsequent attempts under SWNCC 298 to promote romanization (Romaji) were dropped after SCAP and General MacArthur advised that language reform must be handled by the Japanese themselves without foreign directives. The section concludes with SCAP reporting on the Japanese Diet's passage of Public Law No. 245 establishing the National Language Research Institute in late 1948 to conduct scientific linguistic research.

subfiles.about: A New York secretary inquires about institutions and opportunities for studying Japanese for postwar employment.
subfiles.summary: Margaret Neubart inquires where to study Japanese in New York and asks about postwar career opportunities.
subfiles.title: Letter from Margaret Neubart to Undersecretary of State Joseph C. Grew

subfiles.about: The Division of Japanese Affairs suggests institutions offering Japanese language instruction in New York.
subfiles.summary: Dickover recommends Columbia University and Berlitz School for Japanese studies, noting postwar demand cannot be predicted.
subfiles.title: Letter from Erle R. Dickover to Margaret Neubart

subfiles.about: The War Department transmits a CASA proposal on written Japanese to the State Department for review.
subfiles.from: Major General J. H. Hilldring (by Colonel Ray J. Laux)
subfiles.summary: Hilldring forwards a CASA memorandum proposing katakana usage, expressing skepticism and requesting informal State Department views.
subfiles.title: Transmittal Letter Regarding CASA Memorandum on Japanese Written Language

subfiles.about: A military officer proposes prohibiting kanji and requiring katakana exclusively during the occupation of Japan.
subfiles.summary: Lieutenant Robert King Hall recommends restricting written Japanese exclusively to katakana during military occupation. He argues that prohibiting kanji would simplify censorship, prevent access to prewar propaganda, shorten school time, and facilitate typewriter and linotype usage. He predicts that banning kanji for ten years would permanently end its widespread use.
subfiles.title: The Exclusive Use of Katakana as Official Written Japanese

subfiles.about: An internal note suggests acquiring copies of General Piggott's work on sosho for translation work.
subfiles.summary: Internal note advising that copies of Piggott's sosho book would be very useful for department translation work.
subfiles.title: Routing Slip Concerning Piggott's The Elements of Sosho

subfiles.about: The State Department rejects the CASA proposal to ban Chinese characters during the occupation of Japan.
subfiles.summary: Dooman refutes Hall's memo, arguing that Japanese vocabulary relies on Chinese-derived words and homophones that require kanji to be intelligible. He warns that banning kanji is unenforceable and would disastrously impede intellectual and economic life.
subfiles.title: Letter from Eugene H. Dooman to Major General J. H. Hilldring

subfiles.about: The State Department requests copies of Piggott's work on sosho and lists of military Japanese glossaries.
subfiles.summary: Dickover requests two copies of Piggott's sosho book and a list of specialized Japanese language materials.
subfiles.title: Letter from Erle R. Dickover to M.I.S. Language School
subfiles.to: Military Intelligence Service Language School, Fort Snelling

subfiles.about: The MISLS commandant sends Japanese reference materials and glossaries to the State Department.
subfiles.summary: Rasmussen encloses a list of reference materials and forwards two copies of each available item to Dickover.
subfiles.title: Letter from Colonel Kai E. Rasmussen to Erle R. Dickover

subfiles.about: A memorandum transmitting a comprehensive list of Japanese dictionaries, textbooks, and military glossaries.
subfiles.summary: Oshida submits a list of military glossaries, sosho texts, and language aids available at Fort Snelling.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on Japanese Vocabulary Reference Materials with Attached List
subfiles.to: Commandant, Military Intelligence Service Language School

subfiles.about: The State Department acknowledges receipt of Japanese reference materials and glossaries from Fort Snelling.
subfiles.summary: Dickover acknowledges receipt of two packages of Japanese reference materials and returns a signed receipt.
subfiles.title: Letter from Erle R. Dickover to Colonel Kai E. Rasmussen

subfiles.about: Hugh Borton submits an expanded redraft of General Hilldring's proposed letter to George Atcheson.
subfiles.summary: Borton submits a detailed redraft of Hilldring's letter to Atcheson regarding SWNCC 298.
subfiles.title: Memorandum Regarding Draft Letter for General Hilldring

subfiles.about: An initial short draft asking George Atcheson how General MacArthur would view an FEC statement on language reform.
subfiles.from: J. H. Hilldring (drafted by Daniel C. Buchanan)
subfiles.summary: Buchanan's draft querying Atcheson on MacArthur's reaction to receiving an FEC statement of opinion on language reform.
subfiles.title: Draft Letter from J. H. Hilldring to George Atcheson

subfiles.about: A SWNCC reminder to General Hilldring to query George Atcheson regarding General MacArthur's views on language reform.
subfiles.summary: Moseley reminds Hilldring to write Atcheson concerning MacArthur's opinion on an FEC statement on writing reform.
subfiles.title: Reminder Memorandum Concerning SWNCC Meeting Agreement

subfiles.about: A routing note suggesting that ADO prepare a draft letter to George Atcheson for General Hilldring.
subfiles.summary: Emmerson suggests that ADO prepare a draft letter to Atcheson for General Hilldring's signature.
subfiles.title: Office Note on Preparing Draft Letter to Atcheson

subfiles.about: General Hilldring explains State Department support for SWNCC 298 on Japanese language reform and requests SCAP's views.
subfiles.summary: Hilldring transmits SWNCC 298 and 298/1, arguing that simplifying Japanese script through romanization would encourage democratic thinking and eliminate rote learning. He emphasizes that reforms should be encouraged rather than imposed, notes War Department objections, and requests MacArthur's and Atcheson's views.
subfiles.title: Letter from J. H. Hilldring to George Atcheson, Jr.

subfiles.about: An earlier redraft of Hilldring's letter transmitting SWNCC papers on Japanese language reform to Tokyo.
subfiles.from: J. H. Hilldring (drafted by Hugh Borton)
subfiles.summary: Borton's redraft explaining SWNCC 298, noting War Department objections, and requesting Atcheson's and MacArthur's opinions.
subfiles.title: Draft Letter from J. H. Hilldring to George Atcheson, Jr.

subfiles.about: SCAP's political adviser conveys General MacArthur's opinion that language reform should be left to the Japanese without foreign intervention.
subfiles.summary: Atcheson reports that MacArthur and CIE believe language reform should be left entirely to the Japanese. He describes linguistic studies by Dr. Halpern and Dr. George providing objective assistance. MacArthur considers romanization superficial, warns external efforts would cause resentment, and advises against agitating the question further.
subfiles.title: Letter from George Atcheson, Jr. to J. H. Hilldring

subfiles.about: Transmittal memorandum forwarding Atcheson's letter and advising on informing SWNCC of MacArthur's reaction.
subfiles.summary: Cameron transmits Atcheson's reply and suggests informing SWNCC of MacArthur's reaction without circulating the letter itself.
subfiles.title: Memorandum Transmitting George Atcheson's Reply

subfiles.about: ADO proposes withdrawing the SWNCC paper on romanization following discussions in Tokyo and MacArthur's negative response.
subfiles.summary: Schuler proposes withdrawing SWNCC 298 because SCAP prefers avoiding formal directives and MacArthur advises against agitating the question.
subfiles.title: Memorandum Proposing Withdrawal of the Romanization Paper
subfiles.to: William S. Stone, William Benton, Frank A. Schuler, Jr.

subfiles.about: Schuler argues that SCAP will achieve language reform informally and recommends withdrawing the formal SWNCC paper.
subfiles.summary: Schuler advises withdrawing SWNCC 298 since SCAP will accomplish goals informally, while disputing SCAP assertions on language study time.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on SCAP's Position on the Romanization Paper

subfiles.about: A draft recommendation from the State member to SWNCC to withdraw SWNCC 298 and 298/1.
subfiles.from: J. H. Hilldring (drafted by Frank A. Schuler, Jr.)
subfiles.summary: Draft memorandum recommending the withdrawal of SWNCC 298 and 298/1 as SCAP is taking appropriate steps.
subfiles.title: Draft Memorandum Recommending Withdrawal of SWNCC 298

subfiles.about: Confirms General Hilldring's approval of Hugh Borton's January 16 proposal regarding SWNCC 298.
subfiles.summary: Cameron notes that General Hilldring has agreed to Borton's proposal regarding SWNCC 298.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on General Hilldring's Agreement

subfiles.about: An informal note noting the arrival of George Atcheson's letter on the language reform question.
subfiles.summary: Handwritten note informing Emmerson that Atcheson's letter referenced in the attached cable has arrived.
subfiles.title: Handwritten Note Regarding Atcheson's Letter

subfiles.about: Official file copy of Schuler's memorandum proposing withdrawal of the SWNCC romanization paper.
subfiles.summary: Schuler requests concurrence to withdraw the SWNCC paper on romanization following MacArthur's recommendation against further agitation.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on Romanization Paper for Japan (Standard Form 64)

subfiles.about: Official file copy of Schuler's memo advising withdrawal of SWNCC 298 while questioning SCAP experts' assertions.
subfiles.summary: Schuler argues that SCAP will achieve objectives informally and recommends withdrawing SWNCC 298.
subfiles.title: Memorandum Regarding Ambassador Atcheson's Reply (Standard Form 64)

subfiles.about: Borton reports that Romaji will be taught in Japanese schools starting April 1 and concurs with withdrawing SWNCC 298.
subfiles.summary: Borton reports Japanese schools will teach Romaji starting April 1 and concurs in withdrawing SWNCC 298.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on Romaji Instruction and Concurrence in Withdrawal

subfiles.about: Borton advises delaying withdrawal of SWNCC 298 until Atcheson visits Washington in February to discuss the matter.
subfiles.summary: Borton recommends postponing withdrawal of SWNCC 298 until Atcheson visits Washington, noting FEC may raise the issue.
subfiles.title: Memorandum Proposing Postponement of Action on SWNCC 298
subfiles.to: Frank A. Schuler, Jr., Ernest A. Gross

subfiles.about: Transmittal note referring George Atcheson's letter on writing reform to ADO for comments.
subfiles.summary: Emmerson forwards Atcheson's reply to Schuler for comment and suggestions.
subfiles.title: Routing Slip Concerning Atcheson's Reply

subfiles.about: A note recording that an inquiry cable to Tokyo regarding Hilldring's November 19 letter was never dispatched.
subfiles.summary: Note stating that a follow-up cable requesting a reply to Hilldring's letter was not sent.
subfiles.title: Note Regarding Unsent Cable to Tokyo

subfiles.about: The Political Adviser reports on the Japanese Diet's passage of Public Law No. 245 establishing the National Language Research Institute.
subfiles.summary: Sebald reports the passage and promulgation of Public Law No. 245 creating the National Language Research Institute under the Ministry of Education. He reviews the views of the CIE Language Simplification Unit, historical research bodies since 1902, and the expected directorship of Nishio Minoru.
subfiles.title: Foreign Service Despatch No. 9: Establishment of National Language Research Institute

subfiles.about: English translation of Japanese Public Law No. 245 setting up the National Language Research Institute.
subfiles.summary: Translation of Public Law No. 245 establishing the National Language Research Institute. It outlines the Institute's objectives, governance council, operational independence, and personnel quotas for conducting linguistic research and compiling dictionaries.
subfiles.title: Law of the Establishment of the National Language Research Institute (Public Law No. 245)

subfiles.about: An enclosure listing fourteen linguistic research publications issued by the National Language Investigation Commission between 1904 and 1917.
subfiles.summary: List of fourteen publications issued between 1904 and 1917 by the National Language Investigation Commission on grammar, kana, and dialects.
subfiles.title: List of Publications of National Language Investigation Commission
